novel_features.name: Free-slot finder
novel_features.description: Find open time blocks of a given length across several calendars in one query.
novel_features.rationale: Inverts busy intervals from the local event store into free gaps offline; the live freeBusy endpoint only reports busy, never the gaps.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs to actually book something, reach for this instead of pulling every event and computing gaps yourself.

novel_features.name: Cross-calendar conflict detection
novel_features.description: List events that overlap across two or more calendars in a time window.
novel_features.rationale: A self-join over the local events table on overlapping start/end across calendars; no Google API endpoint returns cross-calendar overlaps.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to detect double-bookings before they bite, without scanning calendars by hand.

novel_features.name: What-changed-since
novel_features.description: Show events created, updated, or cancelled since a date, by update timestamp (updatedMin), deletions included.
novel_features.rationale: Filters events by updatedMin (live) or stored update timestamps (local), with deletions included, for a historical window; live-only tools cannot show what changed.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to answer 'what moved on my calendar since Friday?' in one call.

novel_features.name: Meeting-load analytics
novel_features.description: Count meetings and summed booked hours per day, week, or calendar over a window.
novel_features.rationale: A SQLite GROUP BY over the local events table; no single API call returns aggregated load.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to quantify how booked a window is before committing to more meetings.

novel_features.name: ACL audit across calendars
novel_features.description: Flatten every calendar's sharing rules into one who-has-what-access table.
novel_features.rationale: Joins local calendarList and acl_rules; the Google UI has no cross-calendar sharing view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this before onboarding or offboarding someone to audit access in one place.

novel_features.name: Conflict-guarded create
novel_features.description: Create an event but abort (or warn) with a typed exit code if it overlaps an existing event.
novel_features.rationale: Composes the local overlap query with the insert call and returns exit code 9 on conflict — agent-shaped write safety.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent books on a user's behalf and must never double-book.

novel_features.name: Attendee/RSVP rollup
novel_features.description: Summarize accepted/declined/tentative counts per event across a window.
novel_features.rationale: Counts stored attendee response arrays in SQLite; mechanical aggregation no single API call provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to see which upcoming meetings still need responses.

narrative.headline: Every gcalcli and MCP feature, plus a local SQLite mirror that makes free-time search, conflict detection, and 'what changed' instant and offline.
narrative.value_prop: A complete Google Calendar v3 CLI with full CRUD on events, calendars, ACLs, free/busy, and settings — plus a local event store that caches events as you query them. That store unlocks commands no live-only tool can offer: free-slot finding (free), cross-calendar conflict detection (conflicts), change windows (changes), and meeting-load analytics (load). Agent-native throughout: --json, --select, --dry-run, and typed exit codes.
narrative.auth_narrative: Google Calendar uses OAuth2 (authorization-code). Run `google-calendar-pp-cli auth login` once to authorize in your browser; tokens are stored locally and refreshed automatically. Scopes follow least-privilege: read-only commands request calendar.readonly.

quickstart.comment: Verify auth and connectivity (run `auth login` first to authorize — see Auth below).
Mirror your calendars and events into the local SQLite store.
See today across your calendars, offline.
Find open one-hour slots this week.
Surface any double-bookings across calendars as JSON.

troubleshoots.fix: The sync token expired; run `sync --full` to clear the per-calendar cursor and resync from scratch.
You hit a per-user/per-calendar quota; the client backs off exponentially — retry or narrow the window. Prefer `patch` over `update` to spend fewer quota units.
Run `google-calendar-pp-cli auth login` again to re-authorize; check `auth status`.
Omit --timezone to use the calendar default, or pass an IANA name like Europe/Lisbon rather than an offset.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or a terminal user needs to read, search, or book Google Calendar events and wants offline-fast queries over a local mirror. It is the right choice for scheduling automations that must find free time, avoid double-bookings, or report what changed — all with structured output and typed exit codes. It is not the right tool for rendering a graphical calendar UI.

recipes.title: Book without double-booking
recipes.explanation: Aborts with a typed exit code if the slot overlaps an existing event in the local store.

recipes.title: Find the next free 90 minutes
recipes.explanation: Returns open intervals long enough for the meeting as JSON, ready for an agent to pick from.

recipes.title: Weekly change review
recipes.explanation: Lists created/updated/cancelled events since a date, narrowing the deeply-nested event payload to four fields so agents don't burn context on full event bodies.

recipes.title: Who has access where
recipes.explanation: Flattens sharing rules across all calendars into one table before onboarding a contractor.

recipes.title: Quantify a busy month
recipes.explanation: Counts meetings and total booked hours per week.
